title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis
claim: A multi-stage backbone augmented with parallel, scale-aligned auxiliary features that are refined and injected into each block's attention.
layout: 2 panels; left-to-right stage flow, right panel bottom-to-top block detail; dashed zoom
description: Panel (a) shows a left-to-right Swin backbone. An input image H×W passes through patch partition and linear embedding. Four dashed-outline stages follow, each with patch merging and a yellow-gradient Topo-Swin Transformer Block labelled ×2, ×2, ×6, ×2, plus resolution annotations. Below, a purple dashed box holds a gray 'Hierarchical Multi-Scale Topology Representation Algorithm' bar. The input image feeds it from the left. Four small squares with red nested regions (32×32 to 192×192) feed the bar. Dashed arrows carry H/s×W/s×98 topology representations up into each stage. Panel (b) zooms into one block. A vertical stack of LN, Topo-W-MSA/Topo-SW-MSA, LN and MLP has residual additions. A purple-dashed column lists the topology-bias pipeline from Topology Representation up to Additive Topology Bias to Attention Logits. Pastel blue, green, yellow and purple boxes carry the colour coding.
caption: (a) The overall architecture of our Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer (TRiST). In parallel to the Swin backbone, we pre-compute hierarchically aligned multi-scale topological representations at four native scales. (b) The structure of a TRiST block. Each stage-specific topological representation is normalized and refined by the proposed Band-Aware H0/H1 Residual Refinement module, and then decomposed into persistence bands to construct an additive topology bias for window attention. The resulting topology bias is injected into the attention logits together with the relative position bias. Stages 1, 2, and 3–4 use short, medium, and long bands, respectively.
abstract: Medical images contain topological patterns, such as connected components and loops, at scales ranging from small lesions to organ boundaries. Although hierarchical Vision Transformers have advanced medical image analysis, they do not explicitly incorporate topology throughout their multiscale representations. We propose Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer (TRiST), a framework that integrates topological information into feature construction, refinement, and attention. First, a Hierarchical Multi-Scale Topology Representation algorithm computes 2D persistent homology (H0 and H1) independently at four native Swin stages, producing descriptors aligned with each stage's token grid rather than downsampling fine-scale topology. Second, a Band-Aware H0/H1 Residual Refinement module uses gated residual networks to process short-, medium-, and long-persistence information separately. Third, a Persistence-Band Progressive Attention Bias converts stage-specific descriptors into learned key-saliency scores that directly modify shifted-window attention logits. We instantiate TRiST as Topo-SwinV2-B for classification and Topo-Swin-UNet for segmentation, preserving the underlying Swin-based backbones. Experiments on five medical image datasets show consistent improvements over Swin-based baselines and competitive performance relative to existing topology-augmented methods.
